chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Abu Jameela, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It was in the bequest of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) to his companions.'
'Know that the Quran is the guidance of the day and night, and the light of the dark night, in spite of any hardship and destitution.'
'So when an affliction presents itself, make your wealth subordinate to your own selves, and when a calamity descends, make your selves subordinate to your religion.'
'And know that the destroyed one is the one whose religion is destroyed, and the ruined one is the one whose religion is ruined.'
'Indeed, there is no poverty after Paradise, and indeed, there is no richness after Hellfire. Its captives are not freed, and its afflicted are not cured.'
ai.seo_question: What is the hierarchy of values between wealth, self, and religion according to Imam Ali's bequest?
ai.summary: This narration, transmitted through al-Kulayni’s chain, highlights the strategic prioritization of faith during times of crisis, famously encapsulated in the principle 'if a calamity strikes, place your wealth below your selves, and if a disaster falls, place your selves below your religion.' It underscores the Shia scholarly view that material loss is temporary, whereas the preservation of the soul and faith is paramount for eternal salvation. The text serves as a practical guide for believers to maintain spiritual resilience against worldly deprivation and existential threats.
